name: Bellhop dashboard and JSON API
description: Access control for the dashboard and its JSON API, what each page shows, the launch page, tags, throttles and recurring management in the UI, node metrics and insights. Job and recurring behaviour triggered from the UI is defined in the jobs and recurring modules; this module states who may trigger it and what is shown.

entities.name: DashboardEndpoint
entities.description: The mounted dashboard and JSON API.

entities.name: DashboardRequest
entities.description: One request to a dashboard page or JSON API endpoint.

entities.name: LoginAttempt
entities.description: A basic-auth or API-key credential check.

entities.name: ApiKey
entities.description: An API key issued from the dashboard for scripts and the CLI.

entities.name: NodeSample
entities.description: A node metrics sample kept in the store.

ears.if: the dashboard is mapped without an authorization requirement and the environment is Development
ears.shall: allow anonymous access and log a notice saying so

ears.if: the dashboard is mapped without an authorization requirement, AllowAnonymous() was not called and the environment is not Development
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that says how to add authorization or opt in to anonymous access

sources.quote: In every other environment startup MUST fail with an actionable message unless the endpoint has an authorization requirement or .AllowAnonymous() was called explicitly.

ears.if: an authenticated request lacks the permission the page or action needs
ears.shall: respond 403 Forbidden, not 401

serve a dashboard page, JSON API read or MCP read only to a request with view or operate permission, and perform an operate action (retry, requeue, cancel, delete, trigger, pause, resume, edit, launch, change a limit, create or revoke an API key, acknowledge a store reset) only for a request with operate permission

requirements.notes: Applies equally to every built-in page (DSH-13), the JSON API (DSH-9) and the MCP server (BLT-19). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: operate includes view; the view policy alone gives read-only users.

ears.shall: refuse every operate action whatever the caller's permissions

requirements.notes: M1 ships a read-only dashboard (§8).

ears.where: separate policies are configured for view and operate
ears.shall: grant each permission level by its own policy

ears.where: basic authentication is enabled with RequireBasicAuth()
ears.shall: accept only users from configuration whose passwords are stored as salted PBKDF2 hashes

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a plain-text password fails startup (REQ-334), and PBKDF2 is the only supported hash; Argon2 from BLT-2 is not offered (TECH-94). Constant-time comparison is NFR-43.

sources.quote: users from configuration as salted PBKDF2 or Argon2 hashes (never plain text

ears.if: a user, or a client address, has failed MaxFailedLogins times within LoginLockoutWindow
ears.shall: reject further attempts for that user or from that address until the window has passed, even with the right password

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 5 failures in 15 minutes, counted both per user and per client address, so one address cannot try many users and many addresses cannot hammer one user.

ears.when: a script or the CLI calls the JSON API with an active API key
ears.shall: authenticate it with the scope assigned to that key

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: keys are issued and revoked from the dashboard (REQ-337, REQ-338), stored hashed, scoped to view or operate, and expire after 90 days by default (REQ-340). Several keys can be active at once, which is how rotation works.

ears.shall: grant view or operate to principals with that role or claim as configured
show an overview page with live job counts by state, throughput, failures and nodes
show a jobs list filterable by state (including Unroutable), name, queue, tag, correlation id and time range

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: free-text search over payloads is dropped as overkill; tags (BLT-9) are how jobs are found by business key, and every store serves these filters.

ears.if: the store's capability set lacks a feature a filter needs
ears.shall: hide that filter instead of offering it and failing

requirements.notes: Retired. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: with free-text search dropped, no jobs-list filter depends on a store capability any more.

sources.quote: the dashboard hides filters a store cannot serve instead of failing

ears.shall: show a job detail page with the payload, state timeline, attempts with exceptions, interrupted attempts marked as such, captured logs, progress, parameters, parent and children, and the trace id
show a recurring jobs page with each job's next runs and their time zone, last outcome, and the trigger, pause and edit actions

requirements.notes: The time zone is shown next to every schedule (REC-4).

ears.shall: show a dead letters page with bulk requeue
show a queues page with each queue's depth and pause and resume actions
show a nodes page with each node's heartbeat, concurrency and in-flight jobs, plus process CPU, working set, GC heap, thread-pool queue length and worker utilisation with a 24-hour history chart
take a metrics sample every NodeSampleInterval, 15 s by default, write it in one batched store write per interval and keep samples for NodeSampleRetention, 7 days by default
update open pages live through Server-Sent Events and fall back to polling when Server-Sent Events are unavailable
stream the job's captured log lines live, let the viewer search them, and show the job's progress bar, which lists also show
show parent, child and batch relationships as a graph with each job's state

ears.where: a job link is registered for a job type with AddJobLink
ears.shall: show a link from that type's jobs to the URL the application computes from the job
offer every registered job type for launch

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: DSH-12 wins over BLT-8 and the §9 Q9 proposal. There is no opt-in attribute (TECH-96 retired); launching still needs operate permission (INV-301) and is refused on a ReadOnly dashboard (INV-302).

ears.if: a launch form is submitted with values that fail the payload's validation rules
ears.shall: show the validation errors and enqueue, schedule or create nothing

requirements.notes: Fields, labels and rules come from the payload record and its DataAnnotations (TECH-95).

ears.when: an operator submits a valid launch form with Run now
ears.shall: enqueue the job with the form's payload and store the operator's principal name on it

ears.when: an operator submits a valid launch form with Schedule for and a date, time and time zone
ears.shall: schedule the job for that instant with the form's payload and store the operator's principal name on it

ears.when: an operator submits a valid launch form with Make recurring and a schedule
ears.shall: create a runtime-defined recurring job with the form's payload
list recent launches with who launched which job and when

ears.where: a custom editor is registered for a payload type in dashboard options
ears.shall: use it instead of the generated form for that type
show a tags page with the number of jobs per tag, per-tag success and failure counts, and click-through to the matching jobs

ears.when: an operator runs a bulk requeue, cancel or delete by tag
ears.shall: apply the action to every job with that tag for which the action is allowed in its current state

requirements.notes: Which states allow requeue and delete is open in the jobs module (REQ-143, REQ-144).

ears.shall: show a throttles page with each key's limit, current holders, waiting count and recent waits, and let an operator change a limit

ears.when: an operator builds or edits a recurring schedule in the dashboard
ears.shall: preview the next five occurrences in the chosen time zone
show each recurring job's last 50 occurrences with outcome and duration, and its misfire, overlap and validity-window settings

ears.when: a job page shows a failed attempt
ears.shall: show the exception chain with inner exceptions and AggregateException flattened, async state-machine frames collapsed, the job's own frames highlighted and a copy button, with the raw stack trace still available
show title, logo, favicon and accent colour from options, each job type's display name from [JobName(Display = ...)], and dates in the browser's time zone with the server zone on hover
keep insights rollups of enqueued, succeeded, failed and dead-lettered counts and duration percentiles per job name and per queue, per minute for 24 hours and per hour for 30 days
compute each rollup interval on exactly one node, which holds a lease in the store, and write it in one batched write

sources.quote: Rollups are computed by one node under a lease (CON-7) in one batched write per interval.

ears.shall: show an insights page with a throughput chart, a 7-day heatmap by hour, per-job-name tables of p50 and p95 duration, failure rate and trend, and lists of the slowest and most-failing jobs

ears.where: the Redis store runs in ShardByQueue mode
ears.shall: build global views by aggregating across queues

requirements.notes: Uniqueness scope in that mode is INV-500 in the redis module.

ears.if: basic authentication is enabled and a configured password is not a supported salted hash
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that names the user and shows how to produce the hash

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default MaxFailedLogins to 5 (MaxFailedLogins)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default LoginLockoutWindow to 15 minutes (LoginLockoutWindow)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: an operator creates an API key in the dashboard with a name, a scope of view or operate and an optional expiry
ears.shall: generate the key, show it once, and store only its hash with the name, scope, creator and expiry, using ApiKeyDefaultExpiry when no expiry is given

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Creating a key is an operate action, so it needs operate permission and is refused on a ReadOnly dashboard (INV-302).

ears.when: an operator revokes an API key in the dashboard
ears.shall: mark the key revoked

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: mark the key expired

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default an API key's expiry to ApiKeyDefaultExpiry, 90 days, and allow a key that never expires when the operator asks for one (ApiKeyDefaultExpiry)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.if: a request authenticated by an API key tries to create or revoke an API key
ears.shall: respond 403 Forbidden and change nothing

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: only interactive users mint keys, so a leaked key cannot create more keys.

ears.if: a request presents an API key that is revoked, expired or unknown
ears.shall: respond 401 Unauthorized and count it as a failed login for the client address

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (key lifecycle); counting it towards the address lockout follows from REQ-304.

ears.while: no node with the worker registered has sent a heartbeat within NodeLostAfter
ears.shall: show a banner on every dashboard page saying that no worker is running, so enqueued and scheduled jobs will not run, with the time the last worker was seen

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. A cluster made only of client or dashboard processes otherwise accepts jobs that never run, silently (P6). NodeLostAfter (5 min, integrations REQ-411) keeps a rolling deploy from flashing the banner. The JSON API reports the same condition.

scenarios.title: Production dashboard without auth refuses to start
scenarios.given: Environment Production; app.MapBellhopDashboard("/jobs") with no RequireAuthorization and no AllowAnonymous.
scenarios.then: The node is StartupFailed and the message explains how to add authorization or call AllowAnonymous().

scenarios.title: Development dashboard is open, with a notice
scenarios.given: Environment Development; dashboard mapped with no authorization.
scenarios.then: Anonymous requests are served and one notice was logged.

scenarios.title: Operator launches a job
scenarios.given: SendReport is a registered job type; Olga has operate permission; she fills the form with valid values.
scenarios.then: One SendReport job is Enqueued with Olga's principal name stored on it and it appears in recent launches.

scenarios.title: Viewer cannot launch
scenarios.given: SendReport is a registered job type; Vic has view permission only.

scenarios.title: Read-only dashboard blocks operators
scenarios.given: Dashboard is ReadOnly(); Olga has operate permission.

scenarios.title: Invalid launch form enqueues nothing
scenarios.given: SendReport has [Required] Email; Olga leaves it empty.
scenarios.then: Validation errors are shown and no job was created.

scenarios.title: An API key cannot mint another key
scenarios.given: A CI script holds an active API key with operate scope.

steps.note: the script calls the create-key endpoint with its key

scenarios.title: Expired key is rejected
scenarios.given: Olga created key k with a 1-day expiry two days ago.

steps.note: the CLI calls the JSON API with k

scenarios.title: Dashboard warns when no worker is alive
scenarios.given: A web API with the client and the dashboard is running; the only worker service stopped 10 minutes ago; three jobs are enqueued.
scenarios.then: Every page shows the no-worker banner with the time the worker was last seen, and the three jobs are still Enqueued.

glossary.view: Permission to read dashboard pages and the JSON API (INV-301).
glossary.operate: Permission to retry, requeue, cancel, delete, trigger, pause, resume, edit, launch, change limits and manage API keys; includes view (INV-301).
glossary.MaxFailedLogins: Failed logins per user or client address before attempts are rejected; 5 by default (REQ-335).
glossary.LoginLockoutWindow: Window for counting failed logins; 15 min by default (REQ-336).
glossary.ApiKeyDefaultExpiry: Expiry of a new API key when none is given; 90 days (REQ-340).
